decision: Ladybird is the selected first-choice renderer. This ledger records evidence, not release claims. Prism may build selected components or a future native engine only through separate evidence-gated decisions.

evidence_sources.claim_scope: A LibWebView CMake target exists at the candidate commit; it generates IPC sources and links a broad internal dependency closure. This does not establish a stable third-party SDK.
The pinned source has a C++ view-control abstraction; source inspection only, not a successful independent consumer build.
A headless view abstraction is present; it suggests a test seam but does not demonstrate a Prism host or deterministic rendering.
The pinned build instructions document a C++23-capable compiler, CMake 3.30+, Qt 6.10+ and Rust; no build result is implied.

Ladybird describes treating renderer IPC as untrusted, validating privileged operations, restricting helper-process authority and using platform sandboxing. This is upstream design evidence, not proof that Prism preserves those controls.
Servo released a library crate and announced an LTS track; release notes explicitly say this is not a 1.0 stability promise and regular releases may break.
Servo documents an embedding-oriented WebView API. This is a research comparator; Prism has not integrated or tested it.
Servo's embedding overview describes the integration/documentation as evolving and notes build steps normally managed by mach.
WPT is a cross-implementation web platform test project; a pinned subset is evidence of selected behavior, not whole-browser parity.

WASI describes capability-based security, explicit resource handles and avoiding ambient authority. Principles may inform Prism-owned service contracts but do not automatically secure native C++ or IPC.
The current Tauri application hosts Prism UI and native commands; that source does not demonstrate a Ladybird rendering integration.
Prism has a Vello/wgpu renderer for its own paint model; this alone is not a complete web browser rendering engine.

capabilities.notes: Upstream is a browser engine, but no Prism-linked runtime test exists.
Upstream engine components are documented; a Prism integration and capability test are absent.
LibWebView and ViewImplementation exist in source; a stable third-party API/ABI and external consumer build are unproven.
HeadlessWebView exists in source; no Prism smoke-test executable or rendered fixture evidence has been recorded.
Upstream describes IPC validation and helper sandboxing; Prism must verify the actual process topology and preserved boundaries.
The reviewed evidence does not establish the complete set of controls a Prism host needs; each must be inspected and tested.
Crash-related abstractions are present, but Prism-host recovery behavior is not tested.
No Prism-pinned WPT revision, selected manifest or result artifact is attached to this candidate.
This is Prism-owned policy. Renderer-originated requests must be validated by a Prism broker; WASI principles are conceptual guidance, not a ready-made native security layer.

proof_policy: Evidence about upstream code or documentation is never copied into a claim that Prism integrated, tested, or secured the capability.
A capability may be marked verified only when the exact Prism revision, backend revision, test command, test artifact, environment and result are recorded.
Build success, smoke-test success, WPT conformance, security review, accessibility, performance and production readiness are separate claims.
Queued, pending, cancelled, skipped, unsupported and not-run results never count as passes.
Unknown stays unknown. Do not infer support from the presence of a crate, enum, interface, CI workflow, or upstream feature.
Capability security principles from WASI can inform the contract, but do not automatically secure native code, FFI, or IPC.
Changing an engine revision invalidates runtime evidence tied to the previous revision unless an explicit compatibility policy says the test remains applicable.
